chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn Suqat, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Which thing is [such that] there is no vow regarding a disobedience?' He said, 'Everything in which there is benefit for you in religion or in the world, so there is no reneging upon you in it.'

key_terms.حِنْث: Reneging or breaking a vow, often implying expiation
key_terms.نَذْر: Vow or pledge to perform an act

ai.seo_question: When does a vow to do a sin not require expiation?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that a vow to perform an act of disobedience does not incur the penalty of hanth (reneging) if the act provides a benefit in either religious or worldly affairs. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the validity of a vow is contingent upon the utility of the act, distinguishing between mere disobedience and acts that serve a beneficial purpose. The narration underscores the flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding conditional vows, prioritizing the outcome's benefit over the strict categorization of the act itself.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs Bin Sowqat, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zurara who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Which thing is, ‘there is not vow regarding a disobedience’?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Everything what was for you in which was a benefit regarding Religion or world, so there is no reneging upon you in it’.
en.sarwar: 14. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hafs ibn Sawqah from ibn Bukayr from Zurarah who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the meaning of: ‘there is no vow and commitment in sinful matters’.
He (the Imam) said, ‘Whatever is beneficial to you in the worldly matters or the hereafter, there is no violation in it.’”
